text:
An aqueous solution of HCl with pH 1.0 is diluted by adding equal volume of water (ignoring dissociation of water). The pH of HCl solution would

$($ Given $\log 2=0.30)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An aqueous solution of HCl initially has a pH of 1.0, meaning the hydrogen ion concentration is $[\text{H}^{+}]=10^{-1}\text{M}$.

When we dilute the solution by adding an equal volume of water, the concentration of hydrogen ions will be halved:

$[\text{H}^{+}]_{\text{new}}=\frac{10^{-1}}{2}=5\times 10^{-2}\text{M}$

To find the new pH, we use the pH formula:

$\text{pH}=-\log [\text{H}^{+}]$

Substituting the new hydrogen ion concentration gives:

$\text{pH}=-\log (5\times 10^{-2})$

Using the logarithm property $\log (a\times b)=\log a+\log b$:

$\text{pH}=-(\log 5+\log 10^{-2})=-\log 5+2$

Given $\log 2=0.30$, we need $\log 5$, which can be calculated as:

$\log 10=\log (2\times 5)=\log 2+\log 5\Rightarrow \log 5=\log 10-\log 2=1-0.30=0.70$

Thus:

$\text{pH}=-(0.70)+2=1.3$

Therefore, the pH of the solution increases to 1.3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
A person's wound was exposed to some bacteria and then bacterial growth started to happen at the same place. The wound was later treated with some antibacterial medicine and the rate of bacterial decay(r) was found to be proportional with the square of the existing number of bacteria at any instance. Which of the following set of graphs correctly represents the 'before' and 'after' situation of the application of the medicine?

[Given: $N=$ No. of bacteria, $t=$ time, bacterial growth follows $1^{\text{st}}$ order kinetics.]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Before the medicine, growth is first order: $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=kN\Rightarrow \dfrac{N}{N_{0}}=e^{kt}$.

At $t=0$, $\dfrac{N}{N_{0}}=1$, and the ratio then rises exponentially, so the 'before' plot is an exponential curve starting from 1 on the $\dfrac{N}{N_{0}}$ axis; a curve starting from 0, as in (B), is ruled out.

After the medicine, the rate of decay is $r=kN^{2}$, so the plot of $r$ against $N$ is a parabola through the origin that bends upward. A straight line, as in (A), would mean $r\propto N$, and a falling curve, as in (D), would mean $r$ decreases as $N$ grows.

Only option (C) shows an exponential rise from $\dfrac{N}{N_{0}}=1$ together with an upward parabola from the origin.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
Total enthalpy change for freezing of 1 mol of water at $10^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ to ice at $-10^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ is $________$

(Given: $\Delta _{\text{fus}}\mathrm{H}=x\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}[\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})]=y\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1} \\ \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}[\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{s})]=z\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For 1 mol of water the change takes place in three steps; all enthalpies are in J.

Cooling liquid water from $10^{\circ }\text{C}$ to $0^{\circ }\text{C}$: $\Delta H_{1}=C_{p}[\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\qquad (\mathrm{l})]\Delta T=y(0-10)=-10y$

Freezing at $0^{\circ }\text{C}$, the reverse of fusion: $\Delta H_{2}=-\Delta _{fus}H=-x\text{kJ}=-1000x$

Cooling ice from $0^{\circ }\text{C}$ to $-10^{\circ }\text{C}$: $\Delta H_{3}=C_{p}[\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\qquad (\mathrm{s})]\Delta T=z(-10-0)=-10z$

$\Delta H=\Delta H_{1}+\Delta H_{2}+\Delta H_{3}=-1000x-10y-10z=-10(100x+y+z)\text{J}$

Option (A) adds $x$ in kJ to terms in J, so it is not consistent.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: Which of the following compounds is least likely to give effervescence of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ in presence of aq. $\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}?$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A compound liberates $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ from aqueous $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$ only if it is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$ ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 6.4$).

(A) Anilinium chloride, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, is the salt of the weak base aniline; the anilinium ion ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 4.6$) is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$, so it releases $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$.

(B) 4-Nitrobenzoic acid is a carboxylic acid further strengthened by the electron-withdrawing $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ group ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 3.4$), so it releases $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$.

(C) Picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol, $\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 0.4$) is strongly acidic because the three $o$/$p$ $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ groups delocalise the phenoxide charge by resonance, so it releases $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$.

(D) In 3-nitrophenol the meta $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ group withdraws electrons only inductively, so the phenol stays weaker than $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}$ ($\mathrm{p}K_{a}\approx 8.4$) and gives no effervescence.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: The number of valence electrons present in the metal among $\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Fe}$ and Ni which has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the number of valence electrons in the metal with the lowest enthalpy of atomization among Chromium (Cr), Cobalt (Co), Iron (Fe), and Nickel (Ni), we need to examine their respective electron configurations.

Chromium has the electron configuration:

$\text{Cr}=[\text{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$

Based on this configuration, Chromium has a total of six valence electrons (1 from the 4s orbital and 5 from the 3d orbital). 

Chromium is noted for having the lowest enthalpy of atomization among the given metals. Thus, the number of valence electrons in Chromium, the metal with the lowest enthalpy of atomization, is 6.

text:
At the sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is given as nitrogen gas: 70.0 , oxygen gas: 27.0 and argon gas: 3.0 . If total pressure is 1.15 atm , then calculate the ratio of following respectively:

(i) partial pressure of nitrogen gas to partial pressure of oxygen gas

(ii) partial pressure of oxygen gas to partial pressure of argon gas

(Given: Molar mass of N, O and Ar are 14, 16 and $40\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Partial Pressure Ratio of Nitrogen to Oxygen :

The partial pressure of a gas is calculated using its mole fraction. The mole fraction is the ratio of the number of moles of the gas to the total number of moles of all gases.

For nitrogen ($\text{N}_{2}$), the mole fraction $\frac{n_{\text{N}2}}{n_{\text{N}2}+n_{\text{O}2}+n_{\text{Ar}}}$ can be simplified as $\frac{70/28}{70/28+27/32+3/40}$.

For oxygen ($\text{O}_{2}$), the mole fraction is $\frac{27/32}{70/28+27/32+3/40}$.

Therefore, the ratio of the partial pressure of nitrogen to oxygen is :

$\frac{P_{\text{N}2}}{P_{\text{O}2}}=\frac{\text{mole fraction of}\text{N}_{2}}{\text{mole fraction of}\text{O}_{2}}=\frac{70/28}{27/32}=2.96$

Partial Pressure Ratio of Oxygen to Argon :

For argon ($\text{Ar}$), the mole fraction is $\frac{3/40}{70/28+27/32+3/40}$.

The ratio of the partial pressure of oxygen to argon is :

$\frac{P_{\text{O}2}}{P_{\text{Ar}}}=\frac{\text{mole fraction of}\text{O}_{2}}{\text{mole fraction of}\text{Ar}}=\frac{27/32}{3/40}=11.25$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Mohr's salt is composed of only three types of ions-ferrous, ammonium and sulfate.

Statement II : If the molar conductance at infinite dilution for ferrous, ammonium and sulfate ions are $x_{1},x_{2}$ and $x_{3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, respectively then the molar conductance for Mohr's salt solution at infinite dilution would be given by $x_{1}+x_{2}+2x_{3}$

In the light of the given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statements I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II are false
Both Statements I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mohr's salt, $\mathrm{FeSO}{}_{4}\cdot (\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, is a double salt; in water it dissociates completely into its constituent ions, while the water of crystallisation stays as neutral molecules:

$\mathrm{FeSO}{}_{4}\cdot (\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}+2\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Only ferrous, ammonium and sulfate ions are present, so Statement I is true.

By Kohlrausch's law, each ion contributes according to its number per formula unit:

$\Lambda _{m}^{\circ }(\text{Mohr’s salt})=x_{1}+2x_{2}+2x_{3}$

This differs from $x_{1}+x_{2}+2x_{3}$, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text:
[IMG]

Which of the following statements are correct, if the threshold frequency of caesium is $5.16\times$ $10^{14}\mathrm{Hz}$ ?

A. When Cs is placed inside a vacuum chamber with an ammeter connected to it and yellow light is focused on Cs , the ammeter shows the presence of current.

B. When the brightness of the yellow light is dimmed, the value of the current in the ammeter is reduced.

C. When a red light is used instead of the yellow light, the current produced is higher with respect to the yellow light.

D. When a blue light is used, the ammeter shows the formation of current.

E. When a white light is used, the ammeter shows formation of current.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, C, D and E Only
A, B, D and E Only
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the correct statements regarding the threshold frequency of cesium, first note that the threshold frequency given is $5.16\times 10^{14}\text{Hz}$. Using this frequency, we can calculate the corresponding wavelength, $λ$, using the equation:

$λ=\frac{c}{v}=\frac{3\times 10^{8}\text{m/s}}{5.16\times 10^{14}\text{Hz}}$

This calculation gives $λ\approx 581.39\text{nm}$.

Key points:

The wavelength calculated is near the yellow light region. Therefore, yellow light has enough energy to cause a photoelectric effect.

When the intensity of light (brightness) decreases, the photocurrent will also decrease, as fewer photons are available to eject electrons.

Red light, with its larger wavelength and lower frequency, does not have enough energy to cause the photoelectric effect in cesium.

Blue light has a higher frequency than yellow light ($v_{\text{blue}}>v_{\text{yellow}}$), meaning it can produce a photoelectric current.

White light includes all visible frequencies, including those above the threshold, so it will also emit a current.

Thus, the correct statements involve using yellow, blue, and white light, without producing an effect with red light:

A: Yellow light produces a current.

B: Dimming yellow light reduces the current.

D: Blue light produces a current.

E: White light produces a current.

Therefore, the correct statements are A, B, D, and E.

text: The group 14 elements $A$ and $B$ have the first ionisation enthalpy values of 708 and $715\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The above values are lowest among their group members. The nature of their ions $\mathrm{A}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{B}^{4+}$ respectively is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The first ionisation enthalpies of group 14 elements ($\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) are C 1086, Si 786, Ge 761, Sn 708 and Pb 715. The two lowest values, 708 and 715, belong to Sn and Pb, so A is Sn and B is Pb.

Down group 14 the inert pair effect makes the $ns^{2}$ electrons increasingly reluctant to take part in bonding, so for Pb the +2 state is more stable than +4, while for Sn the +4 state is the more stable one.

$\mathrm{Sn}{}^{2+}$ readily loses two electrons to form the more stable $\mathrm{Sn}{}^{4+}$, so it acts as a reducing agent.

$\mathrm{Pb}{}^{4+}$ readily gains two electrons to form the more stable $\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}$, so it acts as an oxidising agent.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: An octahedral complex having molecular composition $\mathrm{Co}\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}_{3}\cdot \mathrm{Cl}\cdot \mathrm{SO}_{4}$ has two isomers A and B. The solution of A gives a white precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution and the solution of B gives white precipitate with $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$ solution. The type of isomerism exhibited by the complex is,
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In this octahedral complex with the molecular composition $\mathrm{Co}\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}_{3}\cdot \mathrm{Cl}\cdot \mathrm{SO}_{4}$, two isomers, A and B, are present. 

Isomer A is represented as $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}(\mathrm{SO}_{4})]\mathrm{Cl}$. When this isomer is dissolved in solution, it reacts with $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$, forming a white precipitate of silver chloride ($\mathrm{AgCl}$).

Isomer B is written as $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$. In solution, it reacts with $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2}$, forming a white precipitate of barium sulfate ($\mathrm{BaSO}_{4}$).

These two isomers demonstrate ionisation isomerism. This type of isomerism occurs when the exchange of ions inside and outside the coordination sphere of a complex leads to the formation of isomers with different chemical behaviors in solution.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

An organic compound weighing 500 mg , produced 220 mg of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$, on complete combustion. The percentage composition of carbon in the compound is $_________$ $%$. (nearest integer)

(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{C}:12,\mathrm{O}:16$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Convert the mass of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ to moles:

The molar mass of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ is 44 g/mol. Thus, the number of moles of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ produced is calculated as follows:

$\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CO}_{2}}=\frac{220\times 10^{-3}\text{g}}{44\text{g/mol}}=5\times 10^{-3}\text{moles}$

Calculate the mass of carbon in $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$:

Since each mole of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ contains one mole of carbon, the moles of carbon are the same: $5\times 10^{-3}$ moles. The molar mass of carbon is 12 g/mol, so the mass of carbon is:

$\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{C}}=5\times 10^{-3}\text{moles}\times 12\text{g/mol}=60\times 10^{-3}\text{g}=60\text{mg}$

Calculate the percentage composition of carbon:

To find the percentage by mass of carbon in the compound, use the formula:

$%\text{Carbon}=\left (\frac{60\text{mg}}{500\text{mg}}\right )\times 100=12%$

Thus, the percentage composition of carbon in the compound is approximately 12%.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: The number of paramagnetic complexes among $[\mathrm{FeF}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$, $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4})_{3}]^{3-},[\mathrm{MnCl}_{6}]^{3-}$, and $[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-}$, which involve $\mathrm{d}^{2}\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ hybridization is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An inner-orbital ($d^{2}sp^{3}$) octahedral complex forms when a strong-field ligand pairs the electrons into $t_{2g}$, leaving two $3d$ orbitals empty.

$[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{5}$, weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$, 5 unpaired, $sp^{3}d^{2}$.

$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{5}$, strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$, $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, 1 unpaired, $d^{2}sp^{3}$, paramagnetic.

$[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{4}$, strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{0}$; four electrons in three $t_{2g}$ orbitals leave 2 unpaired, $d^{2}sp^{3}$, paramagnetic.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{6}$, low spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, 0 unpaired, $d^{2}sp^{3}$, diamagnetic.

$[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{4}$, weak-field $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$, 4 unpaired, $sp^{3}d^{2}$.

$[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{6}$, weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, 4 unpaired, $sp^{3}d^{2}$.

Only $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ are both paramagnetic and $d^{2}sp^{3}$.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift

text: The percentage dissociation of a salt $(\mathrm{MX}_{3})$ solution at given temperature (van't Hoff factor $\mathrm{i}=2$ ) is $___________$ %(Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the percentage dissociation of the salt $\text{MX}_{3}$, consider the following dissociation reaction:

$\text{MX}_{3}\to \text{M}^{+3}+3\text{X}^{-}$

The van't Hoff factor, $\text{i}$, is given as 2. The formula relating $\text{i}$ to the degree of dissociation, $α$, is:

$\text{i}=1+(\text{n}-1)α$

Here, $\text{n}$ represents the total number of ions produced per formula unit of the salt. For $\text{MX}_{3}$, dissociation yields:

1 $\text{M}^{+3}$ ion

3 $\text{X}^{-}$ ions

Thus, $\text{n}=4$. Substituting into the formula, we have:

$2=1+(4-1)α$

Simplifying, we solve for $α$:

$2=1+3α$

$3α=1$

$α=\frac{1}{3}\approx 0.3333$

As a percentage, this degree of dissociation is:

$α\times 100%\approx 33.33%$

Rounding to the nearest integer gives:

$33%$

Therefore, the percentage dissociation of the salt $\text{MX}_{3}$ is approximately 33%.

Thyroxine, the hormone has given below structure


[IMG]


The percentage of iodine in thyroxine is $__________$ %. (nearest integer)

(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{C}:12,\mathrm{H}:1,\mathrm{O}:16,\mathrm{N}:14,\mathrm{I}:127$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 7th April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\to$ Molecular formula of Thyroxine $\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{C}_{15}\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{O}_{4}\mathrm{NI}_{4}$

$\to$ Molecular mass of Thyroxine -

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{C}\to 15\times 12=180 \\ \mathrm{H}\to 11\times 1=11 \\ \mathrm{O}\to 16\times 4=64 \\ \mathrm{N}\to 14\times 1=14 \\ \mathrm{I}\to 127\times 4=508 \end{array}$

$\to$ Molecular mass of Thyroxine $\Rightarrow 777$

$\begin{array}{l} \to %\text{of Iodine}=\dfrac{508}{777}\times 100 \\ =65.38% \\ \text{Nearest integer}=65 \end{array}$
